context: Scrollytelling data visualization — 140 years of global temperature anomalies, with a sticky chart panel and scroll-driven narrative text cards
first_impression: Clean, deliberate scrollytelling layout with strong typographic hierarchy and a restrained palette that feels genuinely designed, not default
what_works: The Tol-derived color palette (warm #EE6677, cool #4477AA) is colorblind-friendly and carried through both the chart encoding and the inline stat spans in the narrative cards, creating visual coherence; the step cards themselves are well-crafted — the opacity fade for inactive steps, the monospace colored stat elements, and the rounded card style all feel considered
what_doesnt: The screenshot captures the initial gray-bar state (step 0), so the chart's most compelling view — colored warm/cool bars — is invisible at first impression, making the opening feel visually flat and monochromatic; the y-axis label is extremely small and tucked tight to the margin edge, and at 11px the axis tick text is borderline unreadable at typical viewport sizes
